description: Transistor ladder filter with fifteen responses, five distortion voicings and a variable slope, plus control over where in the ladder the distortion happens; stereo, or sixteen polyphonic channels

params.text: Sets the cutoff frequency, 20Hz fully counter-clockwise to 20480Hz fully clockwise
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the CV1 jack before it is added to the cutoff frequency
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the CV2 jack before it is added to the cutoff frequency
Sets the resonance; it stops short of self-oscillation
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Q jack before it is added to the resonance knob
Picks the response: lowpass at one to four poles, bandpass at two and four, highpass at one to three, highpass and lowpass combinations, lowpass with a notch, an allpass, a notch and a phaser
Sets how hard the signal is driven into the filter, which is where most of the distortion comes from; a lot of it makes the response types other than lowpass lose their shape
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Drive jack before it is added to the Drive knob
Picks the distortion between the filter stages: Transistor is Moog-like saturation, Fold puts a wave folder before each stage, the Asym settings add even harmonics, and Clean has none
Moves the distortion between the four filter stages: equal gain at centre, more in the early stages counter-clockwise, more in the late ones clockwise; other responses need it centred
Simulates capacitors that are not matched, from exact at the minimum through values typical of a Moog to badly out; it is heard mostly as a loss of resonance
Sets the slope of the four pole lowpass continuously between -6dB and -24dB per octave; the other response types ignore it and the slope lamps go dim
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Slope jack before it is added to the Slope knob
Sets how much the bass is preserved as the resonance rises: fully down gives the bass loss a Moog is known for, fully up removes it
Sets the output level, which is worth having because the other controls change the level a great deal; the lamps beside it follow the louder of the two channels, 6dB a step, with the red one at 7V
Attenuates and inverts the CV at the Edge jack before it is added to the Edge knob

inputs.text: The audio into the left channel; the number of channels on this cable sets the polyphony, and with the right input unpatched this signal is filtered once and sent to both outputs
The audio into the right channel, which runs its own filter with the same settings; in polyphonic mode it is inactive
Moves the cutoff frequency through the trim knob below it, tracking a volt per octave with that trim fully clockwise; it is summed with the other cutoff input, so two modulation sources need no mixer
Sets the resonance through the trim knob below it
Sets the drive through the trim knob below it
Sets the slope of the four pole lowpass through the trim knob below it; an inverted envelope here gives a bright attack that mellows
Moves the distortion between filter stages through the lone trim knob above the row of attenuverters

outputs.text: The left channel's filtered audio, with the same number of channels as the left input

notes: a channel uses no CPU at all until both its input and its output are patched
the six attenuverters come up at centre, so a cable at any CV input changes nothing until the attenuverter for it is turned off centre
menu: Stereo Polyphonic — turns the left channel into up to sixteen polyphonic channels and leaves the right side inactive, at a considerable cost in CPU
